neutral_facts.value: The accused, an army official, was charged with the murder of his colleague. According to the prosecution, the accused reported to his superior officer that the deceased and another individual had abused him. After making the complaint, the accused went to the barrack with a kitchen knife concealed in his lungi and stabbed the deceased on the right side of his chest while the deceased was sleeping. The eyewitness to the incident was present and witnessed the stabbing. The deceased succumbed to the injuries. The accused was initially sentenced to 7 years of rigorous imprisonment and dismissed from service. The sentence was later revised to life imprisonment and dismissal from service. The accused challenged the conviction and sentence, arguing that the incident was due to grave and sudden provocation and that the offense fell under Section 304 (Part II) of the IPC. The High Court rejected these arguments, finding that the accused had sufficient time to deliberate and plan the attack, and that the use of a sharp weapon on a vital part of the body indicated an intention to cause death.

From the Judgment and order dated 25.08.2005 of the High Court of Bombay in CRL WP No. 677 of 2000.

The Judgment of the Court was delivered by H.L. DATTU, J. 1. This appeal by special leave is limited to a particular question only, namely, correctness of the conviction of the appellant Arun Raj for an offence under Section 302 of Indian Penal Code and the propriety of the sentence passed thereunder by the Presiding Officer of General Court Martial under the Indian Army Act.

quotes.text: An FIR was lodged at the Dehu Road Police Station vide CR-26 of 1998 under Section 302 of Indian Penal Code. Thereafter, investigation commenced, during the course of which the body of the deceased was sent for post mortem and an inquest Panchnama was also prepared.
The learned Counsel for the appellant raised two contentions before the High Court of Judicature at Bombay in the Writ proceedings.

We now come to the particular question to which this appeal is limited, namely, propriety of the conviction and sentence passed on the appellant for the offence under Section 302 IPC read with Section 69 of the Army Act, 1950.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused caused the death of the deceased through a deliberate act, using a sharp kitchen knife to stab him on the chest, which is a vital part of the body. The accused had time to plan and deliberate, and the weapon used was dangerous enough to cause death. The prosecution contended that the act was intentional and fell under Section 302 IPC, not Section 304 (Part II).

quotes.text: The prosecution examined 18 witnesses. The General Court Martial after appreciating the facts and the evidence on record, found the appellant guilty of the offence for which he was charged and after hearing his submission with regard to the quantum of sentence, sentenced the appellant to undergo 7 years of rigorous imprisonment and he was also dismissed from service for committing the offence of murder punishable under Section 69 of the Army Act read with Section 302 of IPC.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the accused acted under grave and sudden provocation due to the deceased's abuse, and therefore, the offence fell under Exception I to Section 300 IPC. They also contended that the single stab injury indicated an absence of intention to cause death, thus making Section 304 (Part II) applicable instead of Section 302.

quotes.text: The learned counsel for the appellant contends, that, the death of the deceased was caused due to grave and sudden provocation and, therefore, offence would fall under Exception I of Section 300 l.P.C.

The learned counsel for the Union of India submitted that, the findings of the Court Martial and the punishment upheld by the High Court need not be interfered by this Court as the facts and the evidence on record are enough to prove that the offence committed by the appellant falls under Section 302 of l.P.C.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that the intention to cause death is the key factor in determining whether an act constitutes murder under Section 302 IPC. The court emphasized that the nature of the injury, the part of the body struck, and the weapon used are critical in assessing the offender's intent.

quotes.text: Once intention to cause death is proved, infliction of single or multiple blows becomes irrelevant.

The nature of injury, the part of body where it is caused, the weapon used in causing such injury which are the indicators of the fact whether the respondent caused the death of the deceased with an intention of causing death or not.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence of life imprisonment was imposed because the court found that the accused had the intention to cause death, and the act was deliberate, not impulsive. The court rejected the defence's argument that the act fell under Exception I to Section 300 IPC or Section 304 (Part II).
